subject.title: fix(discord): retry reply session init conflicts to prevent silent message loss

question: Should Discord retain an outer reply-session conflict retry after the shared session self-heal in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101920 is resolved?
rationale: Both recovery layers are technically plausible and affect message/session ownership differently; repository evidence can identify defects but cannot decide whether permanent duplicate recovery policy is intentional.

options.title: Shared recovery first
options.body: Resolve the shared self-heal, then retain a Discord retry only if live proof demonstrates a remaining channel-level failure window.

options.title: Layer both recoveries
options.body: Keep the shared and Discord layers as defense in depth, requiring abort-safe delay, full idempotence coverage, and exact-head live Discord proof.

options.title: Discord mitigation only
options.body: Land only the channel retry and accept that persistent conflicts and recovery policy remain distributed across channel implementations.

recommendation.title: Shared recovery first
recommendation.body: Resolve the shared self-heal, then retain a Discord retry only if live proof demonstrates a remaining channel-level failure window.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest current-main history signal spans both the Discord pipeline and shared session lifecycle, including the closest merged Slack retry precedent.
